children: Shares of TG Therapeutics (TGTX) rose on Tuesday, hitting a fresh all-time high, after the company said the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) had accepted its application seeking approval for a single-infusion starting regimen of its drug Briumvi.
The stock was up 11% at the time of writing, on track for its best day since early May 2026, as investors responded to the regulatory step for the company’s lead multiple sclerosis product.

The supplemental biologics license application asks the FDA to approve a consolidated initiation schedule that would replace the current two-infusion start with one 600 mg infusion on Day 1. Under the existing label, patients receive 150 mg on Day 1 and 450 mg on Day 15.
The FDA has set a target action date of July 10, 2027, to decide on the new application.

The fresh filing rests on the late-stage ENHANCE study, which met its primary endpoint by showing bioequivalent drug exposure between the single 600 mg Day 1 infusion and the approved two-dose start. Secondary measures of safety, B-cell depletion, and MRI activity were comparable, with no new safety signals and no serious infusion reactions in either arm.
Why Does This Matter For TGTX?

Briumvi was approved by the FDA in December 2022 for adults with relapsing forms of multiple sclerosis, including clinically isolated syndrome, relapsing-remitting disease, and active secondary progressive disease. Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a chronic disease of the central nervous system where the immune system attacks myelin, the protective covering of nerve fibers, interrupting communication between the brain and the rest of the body and causing symptoms such as vision changes and motor issues.

Briumvi is the company’s principal commercial product and the main driver of its revenue growth. In the quarter ended September, the company recorded U.S. net product revenue of $232.6 million for Briumvi, marking a growth of 52% year-over-year. The company also raised its full-year 2026 U.S. Briumvi net product revenue guidance to $915–920 million and its total global revenue guidance to about $1 billion.
CEO Michael Weiss said the change to a simpler initiation dosing schedule could further streamline the treatment experience and expand the product’s opportunity in the multiple sclerosis market.
